input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 imposes an MFN/right-to-match obligation on us, the Customer: before engaging another provider we must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer we receive. It is unlimited as to product, term, and comparison methodology, so it falls short of the fallback (defined product, 12 months, reasonable-comparison carve-outs) and sits in walk-away territory as an open-ended obligation to extend Vendor any better third-party terms. It also contradicts Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment. We therefore flip the mandatory operator so no MFN obligation burdens Customer, leaving the rest of the sentence intact; no Vendor-granted MFN exists elsewhere to preserve.

ops.oldText: Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
ops.newText: Customer is not required to disclose or match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have flipped the operator in Section 7.2 so we are not required to disclose or match third-party offers: our playbook does not accept a most-favoured-nation or right-to-match obligation running against Customer, and this aligns 7.2 with Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have given no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment.
proposal.summary: Negate the Customer-side MFN/match obligation in Section 7.2.
